items: As a group, the Flash Family are referred to as "Those Who Ride The Lightning".

While most would assume the lightning bolt symbol of the Flash represents the speed at which the hero can travel. The symbol actually means different things to each holder of the mantle: to Jay Garrick the symbol represents the Thunderbird: the creator spirit of Native American folklore, and how his power was a divine blessing; Barry Allen kept the lightning bolt and added a circle behind the symbol to symbolize unity, that his life was finally complete; to Wally West, the symbol reminds him of a legend in India where lightning is said to be the flashing of the third eye of Shiva, the light of truth.

sections.title: Overview
items: The GCPD Blimp of the Gotham City Police Department is a surveillance dirigible utilised by the GCPD to survey over Gotham City as crime detectors and deterrents.

Outfitted with radars, radio broadcast systems and search lights, the dirigibles assist in suspect pursuits and car chases by providing an eye in the sky to help direct police forces during the chase.

ATTENTION CITIZENS OF GOTHAM... USE CAUTION TRAVELLING IN THE EAST END DUE TO FEAR GAS ATTACK... EXPECT TRAFFIC DELAYS IN AND NEAR AMUSEMENT MILE... POSSESSION OF VENOM NOW CARRIES 3-YEAR MINIMUM PENALTY... GCPD IS NOW RECRUITING, APPLY AT YOUR NEAREST GOTHAM POLICE STATION... BREAKING NEWS: THE MAD HATTER PICKS ARKHAM LOCKS WITH HATPIN... CARMINE FALCONE FOUND INNOCENT IN RECENT RACKETEERING TRIAL... WAYNETECH ANNOUNCES NEW EXOBYTE BREAKTHROUGHS...

sections.title: Involvement
items: The GCPD blimp can be seen flying above the East End district of Gotham City.
A summonable miniature version of the GCPD Blimp, the Toy Blimp, can be purchased in the marketplace for 600 Station Cash.
The GCPD blimp, now acquired by WayneCorp, can be seen docked to the roof of the GCPD Headquarters in the Alternate Gotham City splintered reality.
It can be seen flying above Apokoliptic Gotham City, hijacked to display repeated text of "Hail Darkseid!" However, the version visible in Apokolips: Besieged Clock Tower is normal.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The blimps were introduced in comic canon following the release of Batman: The Animated Series in 1992 where they were included as they fitted into the art deco style of the show.

When uniformed police offers communicate over police band radios, there are many codes and abbreviations used to describe a situation. Codes may vary by jurisdiction, but some basics remain the same; 10-4 means "Okay", 10-20 gives a location, 10-24 means "emergency at station-all units returns", 10-108 means "officer down" or "officer needs assistance", 100 means a "hit and run", 148 is for "resisting arrest", 187 is a "homicide", 13 is for "major disaster activation", and 13, 77 CAPES means "metahuman altercation in densely populated civilian area, call for immediate evacuation".
In the 2016 Winter event there is a base item called ' Scale Model Blimp' which is modelled after the GCPD Blimp

title: Gotham Gazette

sections.title: Overview
items: The Gotham Gazette is one of the largest daily newspapers based in Gotham City with nation-wide syndication across North America.
In competition with the Gotham Globe and the Gotham Herald, the Gazette is noted for producing articles about the Batman and other Gotham-based superheroes and villains.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The Gotham Gazette first appeared in Detective Comics #105 (November, 1945).
Perry White, the editor-in-chief of the Daily Planet, had once worked for the Gazette early in his career.
The Gotham Gazette shares its name with the real-world Gotham Gazette in New York.
The Gazette has live broadcast division, known as Gotham Now!, which Vicki Vale hosts.

Senior Writer in the Gotham Gazette, Simon Lippman is an old-school reporter who has a working relationship with the members of the GCPD. Known for his strict adherence to not revealing his sources under any circumstance, the GCPD trusts Lippman enough to reveal information on a case that they may not reveal to other reporters. In exchange, Lippman may sometimes share information that may otherwise assist in their cases.

Mannheim's Chinese Theater is a large public theater located in Metropolis Chinatown. Decorated in Chinese architecture, the theater possesses a large reception and bar area as well as a sizable stage with multi-level seating.

sections.title: Classic Game
items: The Theater is one of the locations for the first episode of the story arc 'Til Death Do Us Part.; The exterior is the second location for the mission Soul Catcher; The exterior is the location for the side mission Penance.; The interior is the location for the mission Thief of Souls.; The interior is the location for the Mannheim's Chinese Theater walk-in and the Mannheim's Chinese Theater challenge.
The Theater is one of the locations for Booster Gold Exploration Adventures.; The exterior is one of the locations for the mission Explore: Metropolis's Chinatown Neighborhood!.

sections.title: Episode 2: Lightning Strikes
items: The roofs in the Theater block is are a possible location for the WANTED: Weather Wizard.

sections.title: Episode 5: Hand of Fate
items: The Theater's exterior and interior are the locations for the last part of the Unpaid Dues 8-player operation for villains.

sections.title: Episode 6: Home Turf
items: Players can set Mannheim's Chinese Theater as a base entrance with the Eastern base theme.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Although the game identifies the entire block as Mannheim's Chinese Theater, the Theater itself is limited to the central structure in the eastern building.
The Theater used to feature landscape portraits of various Gotham City districts.

If the player looks closely at the "EXHIBITION" poster shortly before entering the theater itself, they will see Greek lettering at the bottom below it which reads, in English, " Online Entertainment Makes The Greatest MMOs". Another sign in the instance has a similar message, when translated it reads; " Sony Online Entertainment makes the greatest MMOs on the market."
While the theater does carry the family name of Intergang boss Bruno Mannheim, the location's exact relationship with him and his family is unknown.

title: Sal Maroni
summary: Salvatore "The Boss" Maroni is a leader of organized crime in Gotham City and an antagonist to the Batman. During a criminal trial, he was responsible for throwing acid at district attorney Harvey Dent and turning him into Two-Face.

sections.title: Overview
items: Salvatore "The Boss" Maroni is a leader of organized crime in Gotham City and an antagonist to the Batman. During a criminal trial, he was responsible for throwing acid at district attorney Harvey Dent and turning him into Two-Face.

sections.title: Background
items: Salvatore Vincent "The Boss" Maroni grew up in the privileged Maroni crime family, headed by his father Luigi "Big Lou" Maroni. Maroni was one of toughest gangsters in Gotham City, and is shown in his prime to be the second most powerful mobster in Gotham City after Carmine Falcone, The Roman. He is largely credited with being the mobster to throw acid at Harvey Dent, and turn him into Two-Face. Maroni owned an Italian restaurant called Maroni's that he used as a front for his criminal activities.

sections.title: Involvement
items: He appears in the headline 'Penguin Marches to Prison' where he throws acid in Harvey Dent's Face.

items: Stacy's is a North American chain of mid-to-high range department stores headquartered in throughout the country. Its selection of clothing merchandise can vary significantly from location to location, resulting in the exclusive availability of certain brands in only higher end stores. In addition to its New York flagship store, the company has designated additional regional flagships in several other major urban centers, including Metropolis.
The company produces the annual Stacy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, a well known parade which is held on the streets of New York City annually.

items: Appearing throughout Metropolis and Gotham City are billboards advertising the company, as well as Stacy's stores appearing in the Cain Street Mall in Metropolis and near the Giordano Botanical Gardens in Gotham.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Stacy's is presumably the DC comics rendition of the real-world U.S. store, Macy's.

summary: For the home of the Amazons, see Themyscira.

sections.title: Overview
items: For the home of the Amazons, see Themyscira.
Themyscira is a location introduced with the Battle for Earth episode.

sections.title: History
items: This location is a portion of Themyscira under attack by Brainiac, as he attempts to escape with the Flame of Change. Two Brainiac ships can be seen attacking from the night sky.

sections.title: Courtyard of the Slumbering Colossus
items: The Courtyard is named after the battle the warmonger Terridus raged against the Amazons, he intended to conquer Paradise Island. He was defeated by Queen Hippolyta, and the Olympian Gods cursed him and his soldiers to become Colossi and protect Themyscira from future threats. Wonder Woman wakes them up during the Themyscira: The Gates of Tartarus raid, and they don't appear again.

sections.title: Paradise Court
items: The Court is named after Paradise Island, the main island in the Themysciran archipelago.

sections.title: Forum of the Five
items: The Forum is the building that houses The Gates of Tartarus, the entrance to Hades' Underworld. It was torn apart by Brainiac when he stole the Flame of Change, and it's the only portion of the map that has rain.

sections.title: Episode 3: Battle for Earth
items: Themyscira is the location for The Gates of Tartarus raid.

sections.title: Anniversary Event: Attack of the Anti-Monitor
items: The Courtyard of the Slumbering Colossus is one of the stages in the Speed Force Flux raid.

sections.title: Others
items: This location would reappear in future DLCs under other names:; Episode 10: Themyscira: Command Post; Episode 13: Themyscira: The Gates of Tartarus; Episode 46: Cursed Themyscira

sections.title: Trivia
items: The story of Terridus and his men are told by Wonder Woman in the Themyscira: Oathbound briefing collection.
In the comics, The Gates of Tartarus are also referred to as Doom's Doorway.
This was the first iteration of Themyscira in DC Universe Online ™. It is also the only time Themyscira is seen during the night.

title: WayneCorp
summary: WayneCorp is a large multinational conglomerate based in the Alternate Gotham City.

sections.title: Overview
items: WayneCorp is a large multinational conglomerate based in the Alternate Gotham City.
Originally created, owned and run by members of the Wayne Family, the conglomerate was inherited by Bruce Wayne following the death of his parents and adoption by Future Lex Luthor.

Merging Wayne Enterprises with LexCorp, Bruce Wayne took control of the Gotham City Organized Crime Family and used the underground to further expand his business empire and eliminate potential competition in the form of other heroes and villains.
